easy.prompt: What is the main purpose of model evaluation?
options: To increase the number of features automatically
To measure how well a trained model performs, especially on unseen data
To guarantee that every prediction is correct
To replace the need for model training

easy.prompt: A model that performs well on new, unseen examples is said to have good:
options: Calibration only
Compression
Generalization
Randomization

easy.prompt: A decision tree has 100% training accuracy but 74% validation accuracy. This pattern most strongly suggests:
options: Overfitting
Underfitting
Perfect calibration

easy.prompt: Which pattern most strongly indicates underfitting?
options: High training score and low validation score
High training and high validation scores
Low training score and much higher validation score
Low training score and low validation score

easy.prompt: Which dataset is normally used to tune hyperparameters and compare candidate models during development?
options: Production data
Validation data
Untouched test data only
Future labels

easy.prompt: In the split shown below, which part should normally remain untouched until the final model is locked?
options: Training portion

Test portion

options: Evaluating a model using one fixed train/validation or train/test split
Leaving out exactly one observation at a time
Training on future observations and testing on the past

easy.prompt: In k-fold cross-validation, each observation is normally used:
options: Only for training
Only for validation
Never more than once in the entire procedure
For validation once and for training in the other folds

options: It sorts samples by feature value
It approximately preserves class proportions in each fold
It removes all minority-class examples
It guarantees identical model scores

easy.prompt: A dataset contains n observations. How many validation folds does leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) create?
options: n

options: It can allow future information to influence evaluation of the past
It always produces too few folds

easy.prompt: Which regression metric is the average absolute prediction error and is expressed in the same unit as the target?
options: R-squared
MSE
Adjusted R-squared
MAE

easy.prompt: Which metric gives larger errors extra influence by squaring them?
options: MAE
Median absolute error
MSE
Accuracy

easy.prompt: RMSE is:
options: The square of MAE
The square root of MSE

easy.prompt: For a regression model, R-squared = 0 on the test set means the model performs approximately like:
options: A mean-target baseline
A perfect predictor
A random classifier

options: It ignores sample size
It converts regression into classification
It always becomes larger after adding variables

easy.prompt: Which formula represents classification accuracy?
options: TP / (TP + FP)
TN / (TN + FN)
(TP + TN) / Total
TP / (TP + FN)

options: Of all actual negatives, how many were rejected?
When the model predicts positive, how often is it correct?
Of all actual positives, how many were found?
How much target variance is explained?

easy.prompt: Recall (sensitivity) answers:
options: Of all actual positives, how many did the model detect?
Of all predicted negatives, how many were correct?
How many total predictions were correct?
How stable is cross-validation?

easy.prompt: Specificity measures:
options: The fraction of predicted positives that are correct
The area under the ROC curve
The harmonic mean of precision and recall
The fraction of actual negatives correctly identified

options: Accuracy and specificity
Precision and recall
MAE and RMSE
TPR and FPR

easy.prompt: What is plotted on the horizontal axis of a standard ROC curve?
options: Recall
Precision
False Positive Rate
Accuracy

easy.prompt: An ROC-AUC of about 0.50 generally indicates:
options: Perfect ranking

Perfect calibration

easy.prompt: A precision-recall curve plots:
options: Recall on x-axis and precision on y-axis
FPR on x-axis and TPR on y-axis
Training size on x-axis and accuracy on y-axis

easy.prompt: A validation curve typically studies performance as a function of:
